name: Midazolam
route_note: IV or IM injection for sedation and anaesthesia; oral syrup for children; buccal (oromucosal) solution and nasal spray for seizures.
targets: GABA-A receptors (benzodiazepine site, positive allosteric modulator)

discovery.by: Armin Walser and Rodney Fryer (Hoffmann-La Roche)
discovery.note: A water-soluble imidazobenzodiazepine: at acidic pH the ring opens to a water-soluble form, avoiding the painful solvents needed for diazepam injection.

tagline: Short-acting water-soluble benzodiazepine for procedural sedation and seizure emergencies
summary: Midazolam is a short-acting, water-soluble benzodiazepine widely used for procedural sedation, anaesthetic induction and premedication, ICU sedation and emergency treatment of prolonged seizures. Buccal and intranasal forms allow seizure treatment outside hospital.
mechanism: Midazolam potentiates GABA-A receptor-mediated inhibition at the benzodiazepine site, producing sedation, anxiolysis, anterograde amnesia and anticonvulsant effects.

Its imidazole ring opens at acidic pH, making it water-soluble in solution; at physiological pH the ring closes, making it highly lipophilic so it crosses the blood–brain barrier rapidly. It is the standard probe substrate for CYP3A4 activity.
uses: Sedation of intubated patients in intensive care
Status epilepticus and prolonged acute convulsive seizures (IM, buccal, intranasal)

history.title: Synthesis
history.detail: Walser and Fryer synthesise midazolam at Roche.

history.title: European introduction
history.detail: Midazolam is introduced in Europe in the early 1980s as Dormicum.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Versed injection is approved in the US.

history.title: Dose warning
history.detail: The FDA strengthens labelling after respiratory deaths with conscious sedation; a boxed warning on monitoring follows.

history.title: Buccolam
history.detail: The EU approves buccal midazolam for prolonged seizures in children.

history.title: RAMPART
history.detail: The RAMPART trial (NEJM) shows IM midazolam by paramedics is at least as effective as IV lorazepam for status epilepticus.

history.title: Glossip v. Gross
history.detail: The US Supreme Court rules on the use of midazolam in lethal-injection protocols.

history.title: Nayzilam
history.detail: Midazolam nasal spray is approved for seizure clusters.

pk.half_life: 1.5–2.5 hours (longer in elderly, obese, critically ill)
pk.metabolism: Hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 to active alpha-hydroxymidazolam

serious: Dependence and withdrawal after prolonged infusion
Neonatal toxicity (benzyl alcohol in some products)
safety.boxed_warning: Associated with respiratory depression and arrest, especially when used for sedation in non-critical-care settings; use only where continuous monitoring and resuscitation are available. Risks with opioids, abuse, dependence and withdrawal; neonates: avoid rapid injection.

facts: Midazolam is the reference substrate used to measure CYP3A4 activity in drug-interaction studies.
